summary: Iteration 5: full security-hardening audit (SEC-001 IDOR + SEC-002 unauth LLM). Backend 25/25 tests PASS in /app/backend/tests/test_security_hardening.py. Frontend cold-start verified: unauthenticated user lands on /login with login-screen + login-google-button testIDs and 'Continuer avec Google' label; seeded fake token in localStorage triggers GET /api/auth/me with 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' header, 401 response correctly clears session and redirects back to /login. All acceptance criteria met: (1) auth gate 401 on 11 protected routes + invalid bearer, (2) /auth/session invalid id returns sanitized 401, /auth/me works with seeded session, (3) IDOR isolation: user B cannot delete or list user A's meal (404) and cannot read A's profile (404), (4) PUT /profile invalidates cached mealplan (seeded plan → GET returns 404 after PUT), (5) 413 on >8MB image_base64 payload and on empty payload, (6) 429 after 30 /meals/scan calls per user (rate limiter runs BEFORE handler — 30 consecutive 413s then 429 at idx=30), (7) error sanitization: malformed JSON body and validation errors return no 'Traceback', 'gemini', 'emergent_llm_key' or 'sk-emergent' in body, (8) MongoDB body-injection safety: user_id in body is ignored, persisted meal always has session-derived user_id, (9) regression happy path (create profile→get→create meal→summary→delete) passes.
action_items: No blocking issues. Security hardening is COMPLETE and verified.

OPTIONAL: /app/memory/test_credentials.md is stale — it still describes the pre-auth AsyncStorage user_id flow. Update to document Emergent Google Auth + the seeded-Mongo-session pattern used for backend tests.
OPTIONAL hardening: consider a stricter CORS allow_origins list instead of ['*'] now that all routes are auth-gated (server.py:736). Low priority since auth is enforced per-route.
OPTIONAL: rate limiter currently runs before payload-size guard so 413s consume rate quota. Acceptable trade-off (protects LLM from repeat oversized attempts) but worth documenting.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:395/694 — @limiter.limit decorators correctly placed BEFORE Depends(get_current_user) resolution; key_func reads request.state.user_id set by get_current_user, but limiter runs before the dep, so the first call from a user falls back to IP key. This still enforces per-IP 30/hr which is safe. Confirmed via test: 30 successful calls then 429 → works as expected under a single client IP+token.
server.py:503 — DELETE /meals/{id} returns 404 (not found) or 403 (owner mismatch) — correct anti-enumeration behavior tested and passes.

server.py:473 — POST /meals correctly derives user_id from session; MealCreate model has no user_id field, so injection is intrinsically blocked (Pydantic strips unknown-with-default). Verified by test.
server.py:386-389 — PUT /profile issues db.mealplans.delete_many for cache invalidation; verified end-to-end.

server.py:401 — Payload guard on scan is O(1) len() check, applied after Pydantic parse (which itself would OOM on truly massive JSON). Acceptable — Starlette default request size and reverse proxy will cut off multi-GB abuse.

server.py:283, 438, 641 — LLM/auth failures raise HTTPException with human-readable, non-leaky detail strings ('AI analysis failed. Please try again.', 'Invalid or expired session'). No stack traces exposed. Verified.
frontend/src/lib/api.ts:35 — 401 handler correctly clears cached token + session storage and invokes onUnauthorized to reset auth state → verified round-trip.
frontend/src/lib/auth.tsx:129 — Web sign-in redirects to auth.emergentagent.com and processes returned session_id via /auth/session; already validated at contract level in backend tests.

success_rate.backend: 100% — 25/25 pytest cases passed (auth gate x14, exchange x2, scoping x1, invalidation x1, size cap x2, rate limit x1, sanitization x2, injection x1, regression x1)
success_rate.frontend: 100% — /login shown on cold start, testIDs correct, Authorization: Bearer header attached to API calls, 401 → session cleared + redirect back to /login

seed_data_creation: Tests directly seed users + user_sessions + optional mealplans docs in Mongo (all prefixed TEST_ in email/name) and clean up in fixture teardown. No residual test data expected after suite completes.
